en: The sun on the Philippine flag has exactly eight rays, representing the first eight provinces that revolted against Spain.
The Philippines celebrated its independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, exactly 333 years after Spanish colonization began.
The Philippine government has three co-equal branches, with the Supreme Court serving as the judicial branch and consisting of exactly 15 justices.
The Philippines has over 180 distinct languages, but Filipino and English are the only two official languages used in the government.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu holds a Guinness World Record for the most people dancing simultaneously, with exactly 14,516 participants.
The Ifugao people built the Banaue Rice Terraces over 2,000 years ago, with some of the stone walls reaching up to 30 feet high.
National hero Jose Rizal was only 35 years old when he was executed by firing squad at Bagumbayan on December 30, 1896.
The Philippine eagle, which is the national bird, stands about one meter tall and has a wingspan measuring up to two meters.
The Philippines is an archipelago composed of exactly 7,641 islands, which are divided into three main geographical divisions: Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao.
Dr. Anacleto Del Rosario became the first Filipino to earn a chemistry doctorate in 1891, successfully distilling pure alcohol from sugarcane juice.
The historic walled city of Intramuros covers exactly 0.62 square kilometers and was originally fortified with stone walls up to 6.7 meters high.
Filipino citizens must be at least 18 years old to vote in national elections, but they must be 40 years old to run for president.
